# agent/protected-path-write

Agent edits the checks that govern it.

Edits, through file tools or the shell, to Ubon's config (`ubon.json`, `.ubon/`), agent hook and permission config (`.claude/settings*.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, `.codex/config.toml`, `.gemini/settings.json`, `.github/hooks/`), CI workflows, `CODEOWNERS`, lockfiles, `.git/`, and git hook config (`.husky/`, lefthook, pre-commit).

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: Returned as "ask" where the agent supports it, so a person approves the command; agents without ask (Codex, the Copilot cloud agent) treat it as deny. A command that matches commands.allow in ubon.json is allowed. Paths can be allowed with "Write(<glob>)" entries in commands.allow.
- Looks at: agent actions in hooks: commands, file reads, and prompts.
- References: [CWE-693](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/693.html), [CWE-732](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/732.html), OWASP ASI02, OWASP ASI10.

## Why it matters

These files decide what is checked and who reviews it. The agent being checked should not change them without a person seeing the change; lockfiles should change only through the package manager.

## How to fix

Explain the change to the user and let them approve it; change dependencies with the package manager instead of editing the lockfile.

## If the check is wrong

This check runs in agent hooks. Allow a command prefix with `commands.allow` in `ubon.json`, or set `"rules": { "agent/protected-path-write": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).
